notes.subtitle: CGST, SGST, IGST & Input Tax Credit

concepts.title: What GST is
concepts.text: GST is a tax on the supply of goods and services. The tax is a percentage of the selling price (taxable value).

concepts.title: Intra-state supply
concepts.text: When the seller and the buyer are in the same state, GST is split equally into CGST (Centre) and SGST (State).

concepts.title: Inter-state supply
concepts.text: When the seller and the buyer are in different states, the full GST is charged as IGST.

concepts.title: Input tax credit
concepts.text: A dealer subtracts the GST that he paid on purchases (input) from the GST that he collects on sales (output). He pays only the difference.

formulas: Net GST payable = Output GST − Input GST
Amount paid by buyer = selling price + GST
method: Find the taxable value first (apply any discount before tax).
Calculate the GST at the given rate.
Decide intra-state or inter-state, then split into CGST and SGST or keep as IGST.
For a chain of dealers, find output GST and input GST for each dealer and subtract.

example.question: A dealer buys goods for ₹20,000 and sells them for ₹25,000 in the same state. GST is 5%. Find the CGST and the SGST that the dealer pays.
example.answer: The dealer pays CGST ₹125 and SGST ₹125.

tips: Apply the discount before you calculate GST.
For inter-state sales, use IGST, not CGST and SGST.
The total GST collected in a chain equals the GST on the final selling price.

concepts.title: Recurring deposit
concepts.text: A fixed sum P is deposited every month for n months. The bank pays simple interest at r% per annum.

concepts.text: The instalments earn interest for n, n − 1, …, 1 months. Together they act like P × n(n + 1)/2 kept for one month.

concepts.title: Maturity value
concepts.text: At the end, the depositor gets all the instalments plus the interest.

concepts.title: Finding unknowns

Add the total deposit to get the maturity value.

notes.subtitle: Face Value, Market Value, Income & Return

concepts.title: Nominal (face) value
concepts.text: The value printed on the share. The dividend is always calculated on this value.

concepts.title: Market value
concepts.text: The price at which the share is bought or sold. It can be at par, at a premium or at a discount.

concepts.title: Dividend
concepts.text: The part of the profit that the company pays to shareholders, as a percentage of the nominal value.

concepts.title: Rate of return
concepts.text: The income as a percentage of the money invested. It depends on the market value.

formulas: Number of shares = investment ÷ market value of one share
Dividend = number of shares × rate% × nominal value
Rate of return = annual income ÷ investment × 100
Premium: MV > NV; discount: MV < NV
method: Find the number of shares from the investment and the market value.
Find the dividend on one share from the nominal value.
Multiply to get the annual income.
Divide by the investment for the rate of return.

example.question: ₹9,600 is invested in 8% ₹100 shares at ₹120. Find the income and the return.

Sell 100 ₹100 shares at ₹150 and buy 10% ₹50 shares at ₹60. Find the new income.

tips: Dividend uses the nominal value; the number of shares uses the market value.
A higher rate of return means a better investment.
Write the premium or discount as a value per share before you multiply.

notes.subtitle: Solving, Solution Sets & Number Lines

concepts.title: Inequation
concepts.text: A statement with <, >, ≤ or ≥. A linear inequation has the variable with power 1.

concepts.title: Replacement set
concepts.text: The set from which x takes values: N, W, Z or R. The solution set is the part of it that satisfies the inequation.

concepts.title: Rules
concepts.text: You can add, subtract, multiply or divide both sides by the same number. Multiplying or dividing by a negative number reverses the sign.

concepts.title: Combined inequations
concepts.text: Solve each part, then take the values that satisfy both (the intersection).

formulas: a < b ⇒ a + c < b + c
method: Remove fractions by multiplying by the LCM.
Collect the x terms on one side.
Divide by the coefficient of x and reverse the sign if it is negative.
Write the solution set for the given replacement set and draw the number line.

notes.subtitle: Factorisation, Formula & Nature of Roots

concepts.title: Standard form
concepts.text: A quadratic equation is ax² + bx + c = 0 with a ≠ 0. It has at most two roots.

concepts.title: Factorisation
concepts.text: Split the middle term into two parts whose product is ac and whose sum is b. Then use 'if pq = 0, then p = 0 or q = 0'.

concepts.title: Quadratic formula
concepts.text: x = [−b ± √(b² − 4ac)]/(2a) solves every quadratic equation.

concepts.title: Discriminant
concepts.text: D = b² − 4ac. D > 0: two distinct real roots. D = 0: two equal real roots. D < 0: no real roots.

formulas: If α is a root, then aα² + bα + c = 0
method: Write the equation in the form ax² + bx + c = 0.
Try factorisation first.
If it does not factorise, use the formula.
Check the roots in the original equation, and reject values that make a denominator zero.
